payload.blocks: Only the start order of plans 261122-0056-orchestration-skeleton and 261122-1950-owner-communication-standard; nothing runs late before heads-stable finishes (phase 11, after 21:06 today).
payload.headline: orchestration-skeleton and owner-communication-standard each wait for the other: which runs first?

parts.cause: The two orders were written separately: the planner of owner-communication-standard put the skeleton in blockedBy, and your later answer put owner-communication-standard ahead of the skeleton. Both plans also share footprint with heads-stable (.agents/skills/**, plugins/fgOS/skills/**, CHANGELOG.md), so they are held until it is done anyway.

options.cost: One plan-file note from me; no planner work.
options.does: The skeleton is admitted once heads-stable is done; owner-communication-standard keeps its blockedBy and follows the skeleton. I record this in the skeleton plan as superseding the order part of q-yoxcjqa46z.
options.gain: The skeleton (p-7pjiqfoj7v, which must stabilize early) can start tonight. It does not wait on component-authority-doors, which is still a draft.
options.harm: owner-communication-standard runs later than your earlier answer put it.
options.label: Skeleton first, then owner-communication

options.cost: One planner pass on owner-communication-standard, and possibly a decision on component-authority-doors.
options.does: A planner removes orchestration-skeleton from the blockedBy of owner-communication-standard; the skeleton keeps waiting as your answer says.
options.harm: owner-communication-standard still waits on component-authority-doors (draft, no lead), so the skeleton waits on that draft too, with no date.
options.label: Owner-communication first, then skeleton

parts.recommendation: Skeleton first: it removes the cycle with no planner work, and it does not tie the skeleton to a draft plan.

scope.allows: Changing the start order of these two plans and recording it in their plan files.
scope.forbids: Any change to either plan's scope, footprint or phases, and any change to heads-stable.

parts.what: Your answer q-yoxcjqa46z (2026-11-22 22:12) says orchestration-skeleton starts once heads-stable, owner-communication-standard and component-authority are done. But owner-communication-standard lists orchestration-skeleton in its blockedBy, plus 261121-2110-component-authority-doors, which is still draft. Each plan waits for the other, so once heads-stable is done neither can be admitted.
